newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke-Buba to revalue fx reserves somewhat higher.
newsitem.headline: Welteke-Buba to revalue fx reserves somewhat higher.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday the Bundesbank planned to value its foreign currency reserves at "somewhat higher" levels in its 1997 balance sheet.

"Until now, we have valued dollar reserves at historically low levels, and because of the recent depreciation of the mark this had led to balance sheet losses," Welteke told German television. "We now want to value the dollar reserves differently -- to value them somwhat higher for the 1997 balance sheet."
"Of course we will continue to value reserves carefully, and then we will consider whether a portion of the profits can be paid out," Welkteke added.
The Bundesbank official, who is also president of the state central bank of Hessen, said the recent controversy between the central bank and the government over revaluation of assets was over.

The Bundesbank law states that the central bank value its foreign currency reserves at the lowest historical level, which is 1.3620 marks to the dollar. The dollar, however, is currently trading at 1.7325 marks.
